public_runtime_contract.threading: one public handle is runtime-serialized; direct internal runtime access is not independently thread-safe

recall_control.shadow: the deterministic System-One controller plans once per recall after the default planner executes; the result gains an optional recall_control telemetry block (request, response, usage, routes_executed, route_candidate_counts, shadow_delta, actual_stop); candidates, admission, ranking and returned are identical to off

source_ref.validation: non-empty string, at most 256 characters; not settable through overrides
source_ref.use: recorded in the fact's immutable write_provenance; read only by the cross-fact guard set (same declared source)

canonical_json_v2.migration_posture: verify_before_recommit; side-effect-free preflight; transactional recommit only on verified disposable copy

write_semantics.self_validity: bounded and anchored only by caller-declared observed_at; may limit, never affirm currentness
write_semantics.proposal_application: explicit caller action through governed lifecycle; never automatic

read_semantics.canonical_admission: single governed admission boundary after candidate union
read_semantics.explicit_current_unknown_basis: time-neutral normalized-content fallback for genuine relevance ties; applicable-over-unknown only inside persisted typed exclusive competition
read_semantics.lexical_anti_laundering: candidate-specific masking only for high-risk persisted self-claims and high-confidence consumed temporal-intent spans

return_budget.rule: returned is the ranked prefix of the admitted set at k; admitted stays whole and is counted; a call without a budget returns exactly what contract 1.3.0 returned

semantic_route.ordering: subordinate: semantic-only candidates order after every relevance and temporal stage; the route never counts toward corroboration and never moves a lexical score (ranking policy 3.2.0; unchanged in 3.3.0)
semantic_route.off_equivalence: with no semantic hit, 3.2.0 orders exactly as 3.1.2 (reference/tests/test_semantic_route_policy_320.py); the facade default opens no representation provider and writes no derived store

representation.provider: pinned local ONNX export, optional extra 'semantic' (decision-embedding-dependency)
representation.config_digest_scope: binds every model file digest, the numerics settings and the onnxruntime, tokenizers and numpy versions pinned by reference/requirements-semantic.txt

semantic_route.eligibility: the same domain-eligibility prefilter as the lexical route

recall_control.actual_stop: describes the default planner's execution: no_evidence, frontier_exhausted, or max_candidates (resource) when the semantic host cap of 16 binds; never a controller quality judgement
recall_control.failure: controller unavailable or invalid response leaves recall unchanged (fallback_events: controller_failure_no_effect)
recall_control.enforcement: none: budgets, deadlines and adaptive stopping are T-controller-2

cross_fact_currentness.applies_to: explicit-current recall only (caller-declared or query_language_explicit); historical, as-of, atemporal and inferred recalls are identical to 3.2.0 apart from policy identity
cross_fact_currentness.label: limited_by_cross_fact_state_change (basis interpreted_cross_fact, evidence cross_fact_limitation)
cross_fact_currentness.condition: a newer admitted fact carries an open, unapplied write-time state_change_candidate proposal against the older fact and guards G1-G13 hold (same actor, same declared source, same scope, direct observations, assertive first-party change sentence under assertion filter 6.0.0, no contradicting declared clock)
cross_fact_currentness.effect: the older fact is demoted inside the existing temporal_applicability_tier stage; it stays admitted and returned; nothing is mutated and the proposal stays open (Option D not implemented)
cross_fact_currentness.refusal: cross_fact_refusal_reason (first failing guard) under explicit-current intent only
